column1: > A node goes dark, and the claim is about everyone else.
> Columns, tab separated:
>   name       what to call the row
>   endpoints  tunnel placement to establish first, as in scenarios.tsv
>   victim     the node whose only NIC goes down. Never cp: this lab has
>              one control plane, and a cluster with no API server is
>              not a scenario, it is the end of observation.
> Each row establishes its placement, proves the full matrix green as a
> baseline, then takes the victim's link down. The survivors must pass
> every pair among themselves within the health check's convergence
> window: losing one node may cost that node's pods and nothing else.
> Then the link comes back, and the whole cluster must return to green,
> which is the returning-endpoint path exercised against a kernel
> rather than a unit test.
> The victim keeps running the whole time. Its kubelet, dialer, and
> containerd never stop; what stops is the network, which is what a
> power event looks like from everywhere else, and the part the product
> is responsible for surviving.
> The two-endpoint rows differ in who dies. The site's transit for a
> node with no tunnel goes through one elected endpoint, so losing that
> endpoint strands cp unless the election moves, while losing the other
> costs only the direct tunnels it terminated.
